name: Take job calls and dispatch crews
summary: Drilling rigs and producers phone the district dispatch desks around the clock for cementing, coiled tubing and nitrogen jobs, often only a day or two before the casing is run. The dispatcher checks the customer's account, which crews are rested enough to drive and work under hours of service rules, and which units are free, then orders the lab design and the bulk cement and calls the crew out. Rig timing slips by hours or days, so jobs are rescheduled again and again and crews often wait on location. Errors come from details taken down by phone and typed into both the dispatch board and the ERP.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people with nine district bases in Alberta and northeast BC and separate 24-hour dispatch lines for cementing and for coiled tubing and nitrogen.
baseline.notes: Fracturing work is scheduled through pad program planning, not job calls, so it is outside this workflow. About three quarters of calls are cementing jobs, including remedial and abandonment cementing. Crew travel to the lease is included here and should not be counted again in the job execution workflows.

trigger: A drilling rig, producer or wellsite supervisor calls or emails a district dispatch desk with a cementing, coiled tubing or nitrogen job.
end_state: The crew and units are on location and the job is handed to hazard assessment and execution, or the job is declined or cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Peaks January to mid-March on frozen ground, falls sharply in spring break-up (April-May), recovers through summer and autumn; 2020 at the low end.

evidence.note: Organisation file splits: about 400 cementing jobs, 50 remedial jobs and 140 coiled tubing and nitrogen jobs a month, plus about 5-8% of calls that are cancelled or declined. The organisation file's driver (all jobs invoiced) also includes about 50 fracturing wells a month that do not come through job calls.

surge.cause: Winter completion and drilling peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Crews booked through the first quarter, then spring break-up (step-2021); the organisation file gives the same pattern. Multiplier tier C.
About 1.8 hours of dispatcher work per job including reschedules; 20 dispatchers cover the desks around the clock, so part of their paid time is idle night cover.
Resolves account holds on about 4% of calls and capacity escalations.
Job review plus travel to the lease for about 450 cementing jobs a month.
Two operators drive each cementing unit to the lease; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Take the job call
steps.description: The dispatcher answers the cement or coiled tubing and nitrogen dispatch line, or reads an email from a rig or producer, and writes down the customer, well licence and surface location, casing or tubing sizes, depths, job type, requested on-location time and the wellsite supervisor's phone number.

error.defect_description: Location, casing size or depth taken down wrong.

evidence.note: Separate dispatch lines for cement, fracturing, and coiled tubing and nitrogen (trican-contact). Times tier C.

steps.name: Open the job on the board and in the ERP
steps.description: The dispatcher creates the job on the dispatch board with the requested time, then opens a job number in the ERP so materials, the field ticket and the invoice can be tied to it, typing the same customer, well and job details twice.

error.defect_description: Details re-keyed differently in the board and the ERP.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check customer account and site requirements
steps.description: The dispatcher checks that the customer has a current MSA and pricing schedule, is not on credit hold, has given a PO or AFE number if required, and looks up the producer's site safety requirements and prequalification status.

control.basis: Credit policy and MSA requirement: no work without a current agreement and open credit

next.condition: credit hold, no agreement or prequalification gap

evidence.note: Producers require a current agreement and ISNetworld qualification before work (ovintiv-suppliers, cnrl-suppliers). Share tier C.

steps.name: Resolve account hold
steps.description: The district manager phones the account manager or credit analyst to decide whether the job can go ahead on a one-off basis, waits for a payment or signed agreement, or declines the job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check crew hours and rest
steps.description: The dispatcher checks which on-call crews are rested: hours worked in the last days and month, days off taken in the 24-day cycle under the oil well service vehicle permit, and electronic driver logs, so the crew can legally drive and work the job.

error.defect_description: A crew short of required off-duty time is assigned.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313) and the oil well service vehicle permit (s.63); Alberta Employment Standards oilwell servicing overtime rules

evidence.note: Off-duty requirements of the oil well service vehicle permit (hos63) and oilwell servicing hours and overtime rules (ab-es-ows). Times tier C.

steps.name: Check unit and equipment availability
steps.description: The dispatcher checks which cementing units, bulk trucks, coiled tubing units and nitrogen pumpers are free and not in the shop, using the board and the maintenance status list.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Match crew and unit to the job time
steps.description: The dispatcher weighs the requested time against crews already committed, rig timings that might slip and the travel distance from the base, and decides whether the job can be covered when asked.

error.defect_description: Crew assigned to overlapping jobs when a rig slips.

next.condition: no crew or unit free at the requested time

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Find capacity or agree a new time
steps.description: The dispatcher calls the other district dispatchers to borrow a crew or unit, calls the rig to offer a later time, or asks the district manager whether to hold a crew over. If nothing works the job is declined and goes to a competitor.

next.condition: cannot cover; customer uses another contractor

evidence.note: Crews booked through the winter quarter and limited field staff (step-2021). Shares tier C.

steps.name: Issue the dispatch order
steps.description: The dispatcher writes the dispatch order with the job details, lease directions, customer site requirements and contacts, and sends it to the service line by email or the board.

error.defect_description: Directions or site requirements missing from the order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Request slurry design and lab test
steps.description: For a cementing job the dispatcher sends the well data and the customer's cement program request to the lab, which designs the slurry and runs thickening time and strength tests with the field water and blend.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Receive cement program from lab
steps.description: The dispatcher receives the lab report and cement program, checks that it matches the job (casing size, depth, volumes) and attaches it to the dispatch order.

evidence.note: Lab design and testing runs in te-cement-slurry-design-and-lab-testing; wait is an estimate of lab turnaround.

steps.name: Order the bulk blend and trucks
steps.description: The dispatcher sends the blend recipe, tonnage and load-out time to the bulk plant and books bulk trucks to haul cement to the lease ahead of the crew.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Supervisor reviews the cement job
steps.description: The cementing supervisor reads the dispatch order and cement program, checks volumes, displacement and pressures against the well, confirms the blend and additives, and phones the wellsite supervisor about rig status.

next.condition: program does not fit the well; redesign

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Supervisor reviews the coiled tubing or nitrogen job
steps.description: The coiled tubing supervisor reviews the program, string size and fatigue life, nitrogen volumes and the wellhead and pressure details, and confirms the crew and equipment needed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Assign crew and units and set call-out time
steps.description: The dispatcher books the named crew members and unit numbers on the board for the job and sets a call-out time that allows for load-out, travel and the customer's requested on-location time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Call out the crew
steps.description: The dispatcher phones or texts each crew member with the call-out time, lease and job, and confirms each one acknowledges; a sick or unreachable person is replaced from the on-call list.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Wait for the rig to be ready
steps.description: The rig or the producer's wellsite supervisor calls with the timing as casing is run or the well is prepared. Rig timing often slips by hours or days, and road and weather conditions can close the lease road.

next.condition: coiled tubing or nitrogen job: go

evidence.note: Road bans on thawing roads restrict heavy loads (ab-roadbans); rig timing change rate tier C.

steps.name: Reschedule crew, units and bulk
steps.description: The dispatcher moves the job on the board, re-checks crew hours for the new time, re-notifies the crew and the bulk plant, and resolves clashes with other jobs that the change creates.

error.defect_description: Change not passed to the bulk plant or one crew member.

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313) and the oil well service vehicle permit (s.63); Alberta Employment Standards oilwell servicing overtime rules

evidence.note: Organisation file notes rig timing changes by the hour and frequent rescheduling; share and times tier C.

steps.name: Cementing supervisor pre-trip and travel
steps.description: The cementing supervisor holds a short pre-trip meeting at the base, files the journey plan with dispatch and drives the pickup to the lease ahead of or with the unit.

control.basis: Company journey management and check-in procedure for crews driving to remote leases (Alberta OHS Code hazard assessment and working alone requirements)

evidence.note: Travel times assume bases within 1 to 5 hours of most leases in Alberta and northeast BC; weather wait reflects winter road conditions.

steps.name: Cementing operators drive the unit to the lease
steps.description: Two cementing operators drive the pump unit to the lease under the journey plan, check in with dispatch at set points and at arrival, and follow road ban and load limits on local roads.

control.basis: Company journey management and check-in procedure for crews driving to remote leases (Alberta OHS Code hazard assessment and working alone requirements)

evidence.note: Road bans (ab-roadbans) and driving under the oil well service vehicle permit (hos63); times tier C.

steps.name: Coiled tubing supervisor pre-trip and travel
steps.description: The coiled tubing supervisor holds the pre-trip meeting, files the journey plan and drives to the lease, where the unit, reel trailer and nitrogen pumper follow.

control.basis: Company journey management and check-in procedure for crews driving to remote leases (Alberta OHS Code hazard assessment and working alone requirements)

evidence.note: Travel times estimated for coiled tubing spreads moving between leases or from base.

steps.name: Coiled tubing crew drives the units
steps.description: Three operators drive the coiled tubing unit, reel trailer and nitrogen or fluid pumper to the lease, checking in with dispatch, with oversize loads following permit routes and road ban limits.

control.basis: Company journey management and check-in procedure for crews driving to remote leases (Alberta OHS Code hazard assessment and working alone requirements)

evidence.note: Road bans on local roads (ab-roadbans); times tier C.

steps.name: Log arrival and journey check-in
steps.description: The dispatcher records the crew's arrival call against the journey plan, closes the journey, and follows up if a crew is overdue for a check-in.

control.basis: Company journey management and check-in procedure for crews driving to remote leases (Alberta OHS Code hazard assessment and working alone requirements)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Record on-location time and hand over
steps.description: Once the rig is ready, the dispatcher records the on-location and standby times from the supervisor's call for the field ticket, and hands the job to the crew's hazard assessment and execution. Standby on location before the rig is ready is common.

error.defect_description: Standby hours not recorded, so they are not billed.

evidence.note: Waiting and standby at a well site is logged separately from on-duty time (hos63); times tier C.

exceptions.name: Rig timing change
exceptions.description: The rig or producer moves the job time, so the dispatcher re-books the crew, units and bulk and re-checks hours; several changes on one job are common.

exceptions.name: No capacity at requested time
exceptions.description: All rested crews or units are committed; the dispatcher borrows from another district, negotiates a later time or declines.

exceptions.name: Account hold
exceptions.description: The customer is on credit hold or has no current agreement and the district manager decides whether to proceed.

exceptions.name: Cement redesign
exceptions.description: The supervisor finds the program does not fit the well (wrong depth, casing or temperature) and it goes back to the lab.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from job call to crew on location
benchmarks.population: Cementing, coiled tubing and nitrogen job calls at a WCSB service company, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Estimate: rigs usually call a cementer one to three days before casing point; lab testing and rig timing changes set the spread.

benchmarks.unit: share of jobs with at least one timing change

evidence.note: Estimate from the organisation file's description that rig timing changes by the hour.

pain_points.description: Rig timing slips force repeated rebooking of crews, units and bulk trucks and leave crews on standby at the lease.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

pain_points.description: Job details taken by phone are typed into the board and the ERP separately, so errors surface only on location or on the invoice.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a WCSB cementing and coiled tubing dispatch desk in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

pain_points.description: Hours of service and rest checks are done by hand across logs, rosters and time records during the winter peak, when crews are short.

evidence.note: Permit off-duty rules (hos63) and tight field staffing (step-2021).

sources.title: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313), section 63 (oil well service vehicle permits), version in force 2019-06-12 to 2021-06-11
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Oil well service vehicle permit: at least three 24-hour off-duty periods in any 24 days, 72 consecutive hours off before returning to standard rules, well-site standby logged as off-duty only if no work is done and it is not part of the 8-hour minimum.

sources.title: Trican - Contact us
sources.supports: Separate dispatch telephone lines for cementing, fracturing, and coiled tubing and nitrogen.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Tight supply of field staff, limits on how fast recruits can be added safely, rising labour cost; prices raised for all clients in Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 to offset inflation; crews booked through Q1; spring break-up affects Canadian operations; extreme cold caused delays.

sources.title: Oilwell servicing - employment standards exceptions
sources.supports: Oilwell servicing (including cementing and fracturing) overtime is paid after 12 hours a day or 191 hours a month, whichever is greater; the 12-consecutive-hour confinement rule does not apply; OHS duties on extended hours still apply.

sources.title: Supplier Resources
sources.supports: A producer requires an ISNetworld PASS grade for field suppliers, a company sponsor before an agreement is set up, master agreements that mostly do not expire but are amended when services or risk change, and invoicing through OpenInvoice.

sources.title: Prospective Suppliers
sources.supports: A producer qualifies contractors for health, safety and environment through ISNetworld before work; registration and qualification do not imply an award.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans reduce allowed weights on thawing roads; spring weights depend on measured thaw depth; local road bans are set by counties and municipal districts.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35); field roles include rotation overtime premiums.

The validator's simulation chooses the cementing or coiled tubing travel branch at s17 independently of the earlier split at s09; the shares (75% cementing) are the same, so averages are right, but a single simulated case may mix the two paths.
Cementing and coiled tubing operators are added because they drive the units to the lease; the organisation file's process map lists only supervisors, dispatchers and the district manager.
Standby on location is a wait before s24 with no resource attached; crew and unit standby hours are billed and recorded in the job execution and field ticket processes.
Bulk trucks travel under fo-cem-bulk-blending-and-delivery and are not counted here.
Dispatcher FTE is set above the hands-on estimate because desks are staffed around the clock regardless of call volume.

The simulated median (about 2.7 days) is above the 2-day benchmark because each timing change adds a fresh rig wait and cementing jobs also wait for lab testing; both the waits and the benchmark are unsourced estimates, so the gap is left rather than tuned away.
